subject: Dedicated capacity request — Acme AI pilot
message_1_subject: Dedicated capacity request — Acme AI pilot
message_1_body:
Hi Vivek / Laura,

Following up from last week's call — Acme is planning a small pilot to run our LLM-backed search assistant in production starting mid-June. We need dedicated capacity for isolation and predictable latency. High-level ask: 16 A100-equivalent GPUs (or equivalent TDP/throughput) pinned to a single tenant pool for the pilot window (June 15–Aug 15).

Attached is our Q2 forecast and a short call notes deck. Key constraints:
- Hard SLA: 95th percentile < 120ms on 1k token streams
- Data residency: us-west region
- Billing: monthly invoice, PO on file

Can you confirm feasibility and a rough sizing plan so procurement can start contract paperwork?

Thanks,
Jordan Lee
Head of Platform
Acme AI

Attachments: acme_forecast_q2_snapshot.csv (CSV), pilot_notes.pdf (PDF)
message_2_cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
message_2_subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request — Acme AI pilot
message_2_body:
Jordan — thanks for the details and the forecast. Short answer: likely feasible but we need to align on SLO tradeoffs, burst policy, and exact GPU profile.

Questions / next steps:
1) Ben — can you confirm the committed throughput (RPS + typical sequence length) and sales pricing target for this pilot?
2) Laura / Karthik — can infra validate if 16 A100-eq in us-west is available June 15 start given current reserved pools? If not, propose a fallback (e.g., 12 dedicated + burst to shared pool).
3) Jordan — procurement: share the PO timeline and if you need a draft SOW or DPA to start legal review.

I'll pull together a short mutual action plan (MAP) and a tentative capacity allocation today so procurement has something to attach to the PO.

- Vivek
VP, Head of Site Reliability and Capacity
Redwood Inference

message_3_subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request — Acme AI pilot
message_3_body:
Jordan — copying the infra and finance leads. Quick sales summary for the MAP and for capacity planning:

Deal snapshot: RWI-4832 (Pilot -> Potential annual committed Dedicated contract). Expected pilot spend: ~$45k/mo if they go with 16 GPUs; sales target for Q3 expansion assumes committed 48 GPUs across 3 regions by year-end.

Committed throughput (from discovery):
- Baseline: 25 rps at 1.5k avg tokens per request during peak
- Expected 95th token length: 1.8k
- Concurrency target: 300 simultaneous sessions during peak

I've attached a mapping that ties their estimated load to our existing pool types (see gpu_pool_mapping_v3.xlsx). Proposed near-term approach:
- Start: 12 dedicated GPUs (pinned) + auto-burst to shared pool for 20% of load (keeps initial reserved cost lower)
- If pilot hits 80% utilization for 5 business days, trigger an expansion to 16 dedicated

Jordan — can procurement sign off on that phased commit? Also confirm if they require an SLA clause for 95th percentile latency.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: gpu_pool_mapping_v3.xlsx
message_4_subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request — Acme AI pilot
message_4_body:
Agree with Ben's phased approach. Quick infra constraints and recommended runbook: 

Constraints: 
- Us-west dedicated pool capacity is tight in mid-June due to previously committed reserved deals (~70% already allocated).
- Cold-start burst to shared pool has slightly higher p95 by ~20ms for large sequences.

Recommended runbook: 
1) Provision 12 GPUs pinned (June 10) so we can validate deployment and warm KV caches.
2) Enable auto-burst with a strict cap (max 20% of traffic) to shared pool for first 14 days. Monitor p95 and error rate every 2 hours.
3) If sustained p95 < 120ms and utilization > 80% for 5 business days, schedule increase to 16 GPUs and notify finance for billing change.
4) If p95 > 150ms persistently, enable fallback model variant with lower sequence throughput per token for the pilot (discuss with product).

I'll add notes to the capacity calendar and reserve a tentative maintenance window June 9–11 to stand up the pinned pool.

-laura
Director, Fleet Operations
Redwood Inference
